text: Splendid.
Well, look at that.
Oh, very clever.
Nobody saw that coming. Least of all the butter.
Problem solved. Rather elegantly, too.
That will do nicely.
Marvellous.
And there it is.
Oops. Shall we try that again?
Well, that did not go to plan.
Back you come.
Gravity, once again, undefeated.
A splash! How bracing.
Into the drink.
Water. Wet, as usual.
Butter has gone all runny.
And Butter melts. As butter does.
A puddle, but a determined one.
Welcome to the house. Everyone playing right now is in here somewhere. Each floor holds one story, and each room has a portal. Stand on one to begin.
Ah, you are back. The house has missed you. Mostly.
Welcome back. Pick a room, any room.
Back again. Splendid. Where to next?
That glowing arch is a portal. Stand on its plates with the right friends, and in you go.
This one is still locked. Finish the room before it first.
Ah, the fridge. Cold, quiet, and, as of this morning, home to one very determined little block of butter. Butter is not known for climbing. But then, nobody told the butter that.
The pantry. Jars, sacks, a mousetrap, and absolutely nothing that wants to help a small pat of butter. Onwards.
The living room. A piano, a great many cushions, and somewhere beyond them, the kitchen. Butter has never been this far from the fridge.
Meanwhile, in the cutlery drawer, Fork and Knife have woken to find the butter dish empty. Well, they can hardly have breakfast without it.
The dining room. A table the size of a small country, a tablecloth, and a serving spoon with ideas above its station.
The study. Books, tape and a cork board. Somewhere out there is a block of butter, and Fork and Knife are getting closer.
Together again at last. Fork, Knife and Butter, on the kitchen counter, before the house wakes up. Now then. Breakfast.
After breakfast comes the washing up. A sink full of water, and only one of you can float. I wonder which.
Night has fallen on the kitchen. It is cold, it is dark, and it is a very long way back to the drawer. Time to go home.
And that is the end. Thank you for playing.
Cold Start. Where Butter's story begins, in the fridge.
The Pantry. Jars, sacks, and one suspicious mousetrap.
The Living Room. Do mind the piano.
The Drawer. Where Fork and Knife's morning begins.
The Dining Room. Bring a friend. And possibly a ladder.
The Study. Quiet, please.
Breakfast. All three of you, together.
Washing Up. Butter floats. The others, sadly, do not.
Goodnight. The last story of the day.
And the cutlery drawer? Empty. Fork and Knife had already gone looking.
And out through the gap under the pantry door. Butter does love a gap.
And there they were, at last. On the kitchen counter.
The butter dish was empty. Butter, it seems, had gone looking for them.
No Butter in the dining room either. Onwards.
Back to the kitchen, then. And who is that, small and yellow, by the door?
Breakfast. Together. Which, after all that, is rather the point.
Everything clean. Everyone dry. Well, nearly everyone.
Goodnight, Fork. Goodnight, Knife. Goodnight, Butter.
Frozen butter does not squish, however politely you ask. Find somewhere warm.
Butter has melted. Undignified, yes, but a puddle can pour through grates.
Frozen solid, I am afraid. Nothing gets stuck into that until it warms up.
Far too cold to smear. Butter has standards.
Butter, smeared on the wall. Fork can stick into that now. A jump pops it back into shape.
Spread on the floor. Knife can turn that into a lovely long slide.
Fork is carrying something now. Throw it somewhere useful, or put it down gently.
One long buttery slide. Run across it for speed. Butter can jump to pop back together.
Fork bounces off wood. Knife, on the other hand, rather enjoys it.
Fork only sticks into soft things. Bread, cheese, sponge. And, occasionally, Butter.
Knife slides right out of soft things. It prefers wood.
Knife only sticks into wood. A simple knife, with simple tastes.
Dictionary
This is the lift. Walk up and it comes to you. Each floor of the house holds one story.
Fork and Knife. Two friends, two players. Or one player, switching between them.
Knife sticks into wood. Face the drawer wall and stick in.
A planted Knife is springy. Land on it holding jump, and off you fly.
Fork sticks into soft things, like bread. Stick in, then jump to climb.
A Fork stuck in the bread makes a very handy step for Knife.
Fork can carry things on its tines. Do try to throw them somewhere useful.
A string holds the rolling pin up. Knife can stick into the pin, jump off, and cut the string in mid-air. Very dashing.
Knife can stand on Fork's head to reach higher. Fork will not mind. Probably.
Too tall to climb, and nothing to climb over. Hold it with Fork, cut it with Knife.
The flour is too heavy for one. Push it together.
The cheese wobbles off in protest. Fork, hold it still, would you?
The sponge is soaked and terribly heavy. Only a frozen-solid Butter could shove it.
Hello, Butter. Shall we go for a little walk?
Frozen Butter is heavy enough to push that jar. Just walk into it. Firmly.
The light is warm. Wait until you soften, then squish through the gap.
Soft in the sun, Butter sticks to walls. Jump at a wall, hold towards it, then jump again. Climbing, the butter way.
Hop into the toaster slot. What could possibly go wrong?
Melted butter seeps through grates. Very little stops a determined puddle.
Butter, a jump at the tiles and a quick smear will put you high on the wall.
Tiles are far too hard for Fork. Buttered tiles, however, are another matter entirely. Stab into the Butter.
Up on the window ledge, something is tied with string. Curious.
Even together, the crock will not budge on dry stone. Something slippery would help. Something yellow, perhaps.
Butter, smear yourself on the floor and let Knife spread you thin. It is for a good cause.
Knife, face the smear and spread it into a slide.
Cut the baguette at the base and down it comes, like a very crusty tree. Fork holds, Knife cuts.
The baguette rocks away from the blade. Fork will have to hold it.
Fork can climb the wicker basket. Knife can stick into the desk and become a rather springy diving board.
That dictionary would fill the gap by the shelf nicely. It is heavy, of course. Dictionaries usually are.
Jump on the stapler. Trust me.
The ruler leans, but will not fall. Not for one of you, anyway. Push together.
Frozen Butter is heavy. Shove the can over and make yourself a step.
Too soft to shift a full can. A spell in the frozen peas would help.
The pipe is warm. Soft butter slides downhill rather quickly. Quickly enough to fly, in fact.
Step on the mousetrap. Yes, on purpose. Hold jump to fly higher.
Under the bulb, Butter melts. And melted butter pours straight through a strainer.
Soft butter clings between the basket and the box. Jump from wall to wall.
Squish under the door. Butter has always been good at leaving quietly.
Butter floats. Jump in, and the others can ride across on top. A raft, of sorts.
Fork and Knife sink like, well, cutlery. Ride across on Butter.
That soap bottle could reach across the second sink, if all three of you push it over.
The shelf is too high. Fork can carry Butter. Stab it gently, then throw it up.
Push the folded towels off the shelf. They make a perfectly good step.
The soap bottle is heavy. It will take all three of you.
The hallway is cold. Frozen Butter can shove that boot over to the step.
Hop up the books to the piano bench. Mind the dust.
The keys play as you walk. Have a little tune. The sun at the far end will soften you up.
Soft butter clings. Climb up between the piano and the bookshelf.
Hold jump as you land on a cushion and you will bounce ever so high.
The radiator will melt you, and melted butter pours through the vent. Every cloud.
At night, Butter freezes solid, and frozen Butter is strong. Even so, the pot needs all three of you.
The stove is still warm. A softened Butter can smear itself on the tiles.
Smear high on the tiles, stab into the butter, and make a step for Knife. Teamwork, of a sort.
An oven mitt, hanging by a loop. One snip and it is down.
Fork climbs the mitt. Soft Butter can climb between the mitt and the tiles.
Home at last. Fork and Knife in the drawer, Butter on its dish.
The table is high. Fork climbs the tablecloth, Knife climbs the wooden chair.
A serving spoon on a napkin ring. One of you stands on the low end, the other jumps on the high end. Physics.
The curtain is tied up with a ribbon. Knife can sort that out.
The curtain is cloth, and Fork can climb cloth.
The handle is stiff. It needs both of you.
